body.text: oṃ namaḥ śrīlokanāthāya / amoghapāśāya bhagavate namaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>! Homage to the glorious Lord of the World (<s>Lokanātha</s>)! Homage to the Blessed <s>Amoghapāśa</s> (Infallible Lasso)!

body.text: evaṃ mayā śrutam ekasmin samaye bhagavān potalake parvate viharati sma / āryāvalokiteśvarasya bhuvane anekaśālatālatamālacampakāśokātimuktakanānāratnavṛkṣasamalaṅkṛte mahatā bhikṣusaṅghena sārdham aṣṭādaśabhir bhikṣusahasraiḥ navanavatibhiś ca bodhisattvakoṭiniyutaśatasahasraiḥ anekaiś ca śuddhāvāsikāyikair devaputrakoṭiniyutaśatasahasraiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛta īśvaro maheśvarabrahmakāyikadevaputrān adhikṛtya dharmaṃ deśayati sma /
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time, the Blessed One was dwelling on Mount <s>Potalaka</s>, in the abode of the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, adorned with many <s>śāla</s> trees, <s>tāla</s> trees, <s>tamāla</s> trees, <s>campaka</s> trees, <s>aśoka</s> trees, <s>atimuktaka</s> vines, and various jewel-trees, together with a great assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s> — eighteen thousand <s>bhikṣus</s> — and ninety-nine hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>niyutas</s> of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>niyutas</s> of <s>devaputras</s> (divine sons) from the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> (Pure Abodes), surrounded and honored [by them]. He was teaching the <s>Dharma</s> with reference to <s>Īśvara</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s>, and the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> <s>devaputras</s>.

body.text: atha khalu āryāvalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattva utthāyāsanād ekāṃsam uttarāsaṃgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇajānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃs tenāñjaliṃ kṛtvā praṇamya prahasitavadano bhūtvā bhagavantam etad avocat* / asti mama bhagavan amoghapāśarājaṃ nāma hṛdayaṃ yan mayā pūrvam ekanavatikalpavilokitāyāṃ lokadhātau lokendrarājatathāgatasya arhatsamyaksaṃbuddhasya sakāśād udgrahītaṃ yena bhagavān (

children.text: AphSū 160
children.translated_text: (AphSū 160)

children.text: ) īśvaro maheśvaradevaputrapramukhāni bahūni śuddhāvāsikāyikadevaputrapramukhāny anekadevaputraśatasahasrāṇi samādāpitāny anuttarāyāṃ samyaksambodhau / asaṃmohajñānavyūhapramukhāni ca mayā daśasamādhiśatasahasrāṇi pratilabdhāni / yasmiṃś ca punar bhagavan pṛthivīpradeśe idam amoghapāśahṛdayaṃ pracaret* / veditavyaṃ bhagavan tasmin pṛthivīpradeśe īśvaramaheśvarabrahmakāyikapramukhāni dvādaśadevaputraśatasahasrāṇi rakṣāvaraṇaguptaye sthāsyanti / caityasaṃmato bhagavan pṛthivīpradeśo bhaviṣyati yatredam amoghapāśahṛdayaṃ pracariṣyati / anekabuddhakoṭiniyutaśatasahasrāvaropitakuśalamūlās te bhagavan sattvā bhaviṣyanti / ya idaṃ amoghapāśahṛdayaṃ śroṣyanti / yaḥ kaścid bhagavan kilviṣakārī syāt sarvapāpāspadaḥ pāpadharmasamācārī āryāpavādakaḥ saddharmapratikṣepakaḥ avīciparāyaṇaḥ sarvabuddhabodhisattvāryaśrāvakapratyekabuddhapratikṣepakaḥ saced vipratisāraṃ gacched āyatyaṃ saṃvaram āpadyate /
children.translated_text: many hundreds of thousands of <s>devaputras</s> headed by <s>Īśvara</s> and <s>Maheśvara</s>, and many <s>devaputras</s> from the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> (Pure Abodes), were inspired toward unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). And I obtained a hundred thousand collections of ten <s>samādhis</s> (meditative absorptions) headed by the <s>Asaṃmohajñānavyūha</s> (Array of Non-Deluded Knowledge). And furthermore, O Blessed One, in whatever region of the earth this <s>Amoghapāśahṛdaya</s> shall be practiced — it should be known, O Blessed One, that in that region twelve hundred thousand <s>devaputras</s> headed by <s>Īśvara</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s>, and the <s>Brahmakāyikas</s> will stand guard for protection and shelter. That region of the earth where this <s>Amoghapāśahṛdaya</s> shall be practiced will be esteemed as a <s>caitya</s> (shrine). O Blessed One, those beings who shall hear this <s>Amoghapāśahṛdaya</s> will have wholesome roots planted with many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>niyutas</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>. O Blessed One, whoever may be a wrongdoer, a resort of all sins, one who practices sinful conduct, a slanderer of the Noble Ones, a rejecter of the True <s>Dharma</s>, one destined for <s>Avīci</s> (the lowest hell), a rejecter of all <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, noble <s>Śrāvakas</s>, and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> — if he should feel remorse and undertake the restraints [of this dhāraṇī],

body.translated_text: Then the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, placing his right knee on the ground, joining his palms toward the Blessed One, bowing, and with a smiling face, spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'I have, O Blessed One, a <s>hṛdaya</s> (heart-dhāraṇī) called <s>Amoghapāśarāja</s> (King of the Infallible Lasso), which I received long ago, in the ninety-first <s>kalpa</s>, from the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Lokendrarāja</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, in the world-system called <s>Vilokitā</s>. By it, O Blessed One,

body.text: tasyaiva tāvad bhagavan upavāsajāpena ihaiva janmani tat karma viśudhyati parikṣayaṃ gacchati nivartitaṃ bhavati / ekāhikena jvareṇa dvyāhikena tryāhikena vā cāturthikena vā jvareṇa evaṃ saptāhikena vā jvareṇa / akṣiśūlena vā dantaśūlena vā karṇaśūlena vā nāsāśūlena vā dantoṣṭhaśūlena vā jivhāśūlena vā tāluśūlena vā hṛdayaśūlena vā udaraśūlena vā pārśvaśūlena vā kaṭiśūlena vā aṅgaśūlena vā pratyaṅgaśūlena vā arśagrahaṇīśūlena vā atisāreṇa vā hastapādavedanayā vā śirorujā vā balāhakacitrakuṣṭhavicarcikākiṭibhabhagandaralohaliṅgagalagrahavisphoṭakāpasmārakākhordākhyair vā kṛtāpakṛtyair māraṇabandhanatāḍanatarjanabhūtākhyānair (

children.text: AphSū 161
children.translated_text: (AphSū 161)

children.text: ) vā / saṃkṣepato bhagavan kāyapīḍayā vā cittapīḍayā vā dusvapnadarśanena vā tat karma parikṣayaṃ gacchati / paryavadānaṃ gacchati / prāg eva śuddhasattvānāṃ śraddhādhimuktikānāṃ yadi bhagavan catasraḥ parṣadaś catvāro varṇaḥ māyā imadhyanāpi ya idaṃ madīyam amoghapāśahṛdayaṃ śroṣyati udgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati likhiṣyati likhāpayiṣyati paryavāpsyati anyeṣāṃ ca sattvānāṃ śrāvayiṣyati antas tiryagyonigatānāṃ vā sattvānāṃ karṇapūṭe sthitvā karṇajāpaṃ dāsyati / imāni ca mantrapadāni cintayiṣyati / apratikṣepataḥ arūpataḥ avikalpataḥ asaṃprabhavataḥ aciram agamataḥ akaraṇataḥ niḥkleśataḥ samacittanikṣepataḥ virahitapañcaskandhaḥ / anena yogena buddhānusmṛtir bhāvayitavyā / tad eṣāṃ daśabhyo digbhyo buddhasahasraṃ saṃmukhaṃ darśanaṃ kariṣyanti / atyayadeśanāṃ ca kariṣyati / peyālam* / yāvat pustakalikhitaṃ kṛtvā gṛhe sthāpayiṣyati / kiṃ bahunā bhagavann anyonyaspardhayā vā śroṣyati / svāmibhayena vā parānuvṛttyā vā uccagghanahetunā vā śroṣyanti / jñātavyaṃ bhagavan paṇḍitenāryāvalokiteśvarasyānubhāvena teṣāṃ karṇapuṭe sthitvā sa śabdo nipatiṣyati /
children.translated_text: ) or; in brief, O Blessed One, through bodily affliction, or mental affliction, or the seeing of a bad dream, that <s>karma</s> reaches exhaustion and reaches purification — and even more so for those of pure nature and of faithful conviction. If, O Blessed One, the four assemblies and the four castes — even in the midst of illusory affairs — whoever shall hear this my <s>Amoghapāśahṛdaya</s>, shall take it up, retain it, recite it, write it, cause it to be written, master it, and shall cause other beings to hear it, or, standing at the ear-opening of beings even among those born in the animal realm, shall give a whispered recitation into the ear, and shall reflect upon these <s>mantrapadas</s> (mantra-words) — without rejection, without form, without conceptual construction, without arising [of defilement], without delay, without [further] doing, without affliction, with even-minded composure, free from the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates): by this <s>yoga</s> the recollection of the <s>Buddhas</s> (<s>buddhānusmṛti</s>) should be cultivated. Then a thousand <s>Buddhas</s> from the ten directions will show their face-to-face appearance to these [beings], and one will make confession of transgressions. And so on. As far as, having made a written book, one shall keep it in the house. What more, O Blessed One — whether one shall hear it out of mutual rivalry, or out of fear of a master, or out of compliance with others, or for the sake of mockery, they shall hear it. It should be known, O Blessed One, by the wise one, that through the power of the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, standing at their ear-opening, that sound shall fall [into their ears].

body.translated_text: for him, O Blessed One, through the fasting observance and recitation in this very life, that <s>karma</s> is purified, reaches exhaustion, and is averted — whether [it manifests as] a quotidian fever, a two-day fever, a three-day fever, a four-day fever, or a seven-day fever; or eye-pain, toothache, earache, nose-pain, lip-and-tooth pain, tongue-pain, palate-pain, heart-pain, stomach-pain, side-pain, hip-pain, limb-pain, joint-pain, hemorrhoid or bowel pain, diarrhea, hand-and-foot pain, or headache; or diseases named <s>balāhaka</s>, <s>citrakuṣṭha</s>, <s>vicarcikā</s>, <s>kiṭibha</s>, fistula, <s>lohaliṅga</s>, throat-seizure, boils, epilepsy, or <s>kākhorda</s> sorcery; or afflictions caused by sorcery — killing, binding, striking, threatening, or ghost-enchantments —

body.text: tadyathāpi nāma bhagavan kaścid eva puruṣaś candanaṃ vā karpūraṃ vā kesaraṃ vā kastūrikāṃ vā ākṛṣya paribhāṣya śilāyāṃ vā bhūmau vā piṣṭvā ātmānaṃ lepayet* / na ca tasya candanasya karpūrasya kesarasya kastūrikāyāś caivaṃ bhavati anenāham ākṛṣṭaḥ paribhāṣito vā gandhenātikramiṣyāmīti / api ca sugandha eva saḥ / evam eva bhagavann idaṃ madīyam amoghapāśahṛdayaṃ yaḥ kaścid uccaghana vā ullāpya / peyālam* / (

children.text: AphSū 162
children.translated_text: AphSū 162

children.text: ) yāvat* māyāśabdenāpātheyenāpi pūjayet* / teṣāṃ bhagavan khaṭukāṃ sattvānāṃ sa eva kuśalahetur bhaviṣyati / yatra yatropapatsyante tatra tatra avirahitāś ca bhaviṣyanti śīlasamādhiprajñāpuṇyasaṃbhāragandhena / śīlasaugandhikam eva karoti / yaḥ kaścid bhagavan kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bhikṣur vā bhikṣuṇī vā upāśako vā upāśikā vā tadanyo vā kaścit sattvaḥ amoghapāśahṛdayam uddiṣya śuklāṣṭamyām upavāsaṃ kuryāt* / saptavārān amoghapāśahṛdayam anālāpataḥ āvartayet* tasya bhagavan dṛṣṭa eva dharmā viṃśatir anuśaṃsāḥ pratikāṃkṣitavyāḥ / katame viṃśati? yaduta rogāś cāsya kāye notpatsyante / utpannāś cāsya rogāḥ karmavaśena śīghraṃ prasamaṃ yāsyanti / snigdhamanojñaślakṣṇagātraś ca bhaviṣyati / bahujanapriyaś ca bhaviṣyati / guhyārthapratilambhaś cāsya bhaviṣyanti / utpannāś cāsyārthaṃ na caurā pratimocayanti / agninā dahyate / nodakena hrīyate / na rājā śaknoti manasāpahartum* / karmāntāś cāsya sphītā bhaviṣyanti / nāśaninodakabhayaṃ bhaviṣyati / na vātavṛṣṭibhayaṃ bhaviṣyati / saptavārān amoghapāśahṛdayena bhasmodakaṃ vā parijapya digvidig adha ūrdhvaś ca kṣetrasya bandho dātavyaḥ / sarvopadravopaśamiṣyati / na caujohārā ojo 'pahartuṃ śaknuvanti / sarvasattvānāṃ ca priyo bhaviṣyati mana-āpaś ca bhaviṣyati / na cāsya śatrubhayaṃ bhaviṣyati / utpannaś cāsya śatrubhayaṃ śīghraṃ praśamaṃ yāsyati / na cāsya manuṣyabhayaṃ bhaviṣyati / na ca kākhordabhayaṃ na ca ḍākinībhayaṃ na ca tīvrāḥ kleśopakleśā bhaviṣyanti / nāgninā na viṣeṇa na śastreṇa kālaṃ kariṣyanti / yatra yatropapatsyante tatra tatrāvirahitāś ca bhaviṣyanti maitrīkaruṇāmuditopekṣayā / ime viṃśatir anuśaṃsāḥ pratikāṃkṣitavyāḥ /
children.translated_text: ) as far as one should worship it even with an illusory sound or with a worthless [offering] — for those harsh beings, O Blessed One, that very [act] will become a cause of merit. Wherever they shall be reborn, there they shall never be deprived of the fragrance of the accumulation of <s>śīla</s> (moral discipline), <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), and <s>puṇya</s> (merit); it produces the very perfume of <s>śīla</s>. Whoever, O Blessed One — whether a son of good family or a daughter of good family, a monk or a nun, a layman or a laywoman, or any other being — should, dedicating it to the <s>Amoghapāśahṛdaya</s>, undertake the fasting observance on the eighth day of the bright fortnight, and should recite the <s>Amoghapāśahṛdaya</s> seven times without [other] speech: for him, O Blessed One, twenty benefits are to be expected in this very visible world. Which twenty? Namely: diseases shall not arise in his body; and diseases that have arisen in him through the power of <s>karma</s> shall quickly come to pacification; and he shall be of smooth, pleasing, and soft body; and he shall be dear to many people; and he shall obtain the attainment of hidden meanings; and thieves shall not carry off what he has acquired, nor shall it be burned by fire, nor carried off by water, nor shall a king be able to seize it even in thought; and his undertakings shall be flourishing; and there shall be no fear of lightning or flood; and there shall be no fear of wind and rain. Having consecrated ash-water seven times with the <s>Amoghapāśahṛdaya</s>, a boundary of the field should be set in the directions, the intermediate directions, below, and above — all calamities shall be pacified. And the <s>ojohāras</s> (vitality-stealers) shall not be able to steal away [his] vitality; and he shall be dear and pleasing to all beings; and he shall have no fear of enemies, and any fear of enemies that has arisen for him shall quickly come to pacification; and he shall have no fear of human beings, nor fear of <s>kākhorda</s> (sorcery), nor fear of <s>ḍākinīs</s>, nor shall there be fierce afflictions and secondary afflictions; they shall not die by fire, by poison, or by weapon; and wherever they shall be reborn, there they shall never be deprived of loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity. These twenty benefits are to be expected.

body.translated_text: It is just as, O Blessed One, when some man, having drawn out <s>candana</s> (sandalwood), or <s>karpūra</s> (camphor), or <s>kesara</s> (saffron), or <s>kastūrikā</s> (musk), and having ground it upon a stone or on the ground, should anoint himself with it. And it does not occur to that <s>candana</s>, <s>karpūra</s>, <s>kesara</s>, or <s>kastūrikā</s>: 'By this one I have been drawn out and ground up; I shall overpower [him] with my fragrance.' Yet it is fragrant all the same. Just so, O Blessed One, this my <s>Amoghapāśahṛdaya</s> — whoever, whether in mockery or by way of jesting. And so on. (

body.text: aparān aṣṭau dharmān pratilapsyante / katamān aṣṭau? maraṇakāle āryāvalokiteśvaro bhikṣurūpeṇa saṃmukhaṃ darśanaṃ dāsyati / sukhena kālaṃ kariṣyati / na bhrāntadṛṣṭir (

children.text: AphSū 163
children.translated_text: AphSū 163

children.text: ) bhaviṣyati / na hastavikṣepaṃ kariṣyati / na pādavikṣepaṃ noccāraṃ na prasrāvaṃ na cārūḍhaḥ kālaṃ kariṣyati / supratiṣṭhitasmṛtir bhaviṣyati / nādhomukhaḥ kālaṃ kariṣyati / maraṇakāle 'kṣayapratibhānaṃ cāsya bhaviṣyati / yatra yatra cāsya buddhakṣetre praṇidhis tatra tatropapattir bhaviṣyati / avirahitaś ca bhaviṣyati kalyāṇamitraiḥ / dine dine trikālaṃ trīṇi vārān āvartayitavyam* / madyamāṃsapalāṇḍuguñjanakalaśunaśaṃkārakṛtocchiṣṭaviśeṣārthino hy etad varjyaḥ / ayaṃ cāmoghapāśahṛdayaṃ nāma dharmaparyāyaḥ sarvasattvānāṃ balābalaṃ jñātvā śroṣayitavyaḥ / ācāryamuṣṭir na kartavyā / yasmād dhi gate malamātsaryerṣyāpagato bodhisattvā bhavanti / sattvānām arthakaraṇena bodhiḥ prāpyate bodhisattvānāṃ gaṇanāṃś ca gacchanti / bodhir ity ucyate prajñāsattva upāyaḥ / etau dvau dharmau sattvānām arthakaraṇenaiva prāpyete / sacen me bhagavann anujānīyād yan nv aham imaṃ hṛdayaṃ tathāgatasya purataḥ kīrtaye catasṛṇāṃ parṣadām arthāya hitāya sukhāyānyeṣāṃ ca pāpakāriṇām* /
children.translated_text: ) and shall not throw about the hands; one shall not throw about the feet, nor [pass] excrement nor urine, nor die while sitting upright; one shall have well-established mindfulness; one shall not die face-downward; and at the time of death one shall have inexhaustible eloquence; and in whatever <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (Buddha-field) one's aspiration is directed, there one shall be reborn; and one shall never be deprived of spiritual friends (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>). Day after day, at the three times, it should be recited three times. But those who seek wine, meat, onion, <s>guñjana</s>, garlic, refuse, leftover food, and the like are to be excluded from this. And this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse named <s>Amoghapāśahṛdaya</s> should be taught to all beings after assessing their strength or weakness. One should not make a teacher's fist [withholding the teaching]. For, when [such withholding] is gone, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> become free of taint, miserliness, and envy. Through accomplishing the welfare of beings, awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) is attained, and they come to be counted among the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. <s>Bodhi</s> is said [to be] <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom); <s>sattva</s> is <s>upāya</s> (skillful means). These two qualities are attained precisely through accomplishing the welfare of beings. If, O Blessed One, you would permit me, then I would proclaim this Heart [dhāraṇī] before the <s>Tathāgata</s>, for the sake, benefit, and happiness of the four assemblies, and of other wrongdoers as well.

body.translated_text: They shall obtain another eight qualities. Which eight? At the time of death, the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> will show his face-to-face appearance in the form of a monk; one shall die with ease; one shall not have deluded vision (

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān āryāvalokiteśvaro bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvam etad avocat* / bhāṣasva śuddhasattvāya yasyedānīṃ kālaṃ manyase / anumoditaṃ tathāgatena paścimakāle paścimasamaye bodhisattvayānikānāṃ pitṛkāryaṃ kariṣyati /
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One spoke thus to the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>: 'Speak, for the sake of beings of pure nature, [the teaching] whose time you now think [is right]. It is approved by the <s>Tathāgata</s>; in the latter time, in the latter age, it will accomplish the fatherly task for those of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> vehicle.'

body.text: atha khalu āryāvalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'nimiṣanayano bhūtvā bhagavantam etad avocat* / śṛṇu me bhagavan sarvabuddhabodhisattvanamaskṛtam idaṃ vimokṣamukhamaṇḍalaṃ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya mahato janakāyasyārthāya hitāya sukhāya vimokṣārthāya / nāmas tryadhvānugatapratiṣṭhitebhyaḥ sarvabuddhabodhisattvebhyaḥ / namaḥ pratyekabuddhāryaśrāvakasaṃghebhyo 'tītānāgatapratyutpannebhyaḥ / namaḥ samyaggatānām* / (

children.translated_text: (AphSū 164)

children.text: ) namaḥ samyakpratipannānām* / namaḥ śāradvatīputrāya mahāmataye / namaḥ āryamaitreyapramukhebhyo mahābodhisattvasaṃghebhyaḥ / namaḥ supratiṣṭhitaśailendrarājapramukhebhyaḥ tathāgatebhyo 'rhadbhyaḥ samyakasaṃbuddhebhyo bhagavadbhyaḥ / namaḥ suvarṇavarṇasupratibhāsavinivartiteśvararājāya tathāgatāya / namaḥ siṃhavikrīḍitarājāya tathāgatāya / namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya / namaḥ supratiṣṭhitamaṇikūṭarājāya tathāgatāya / namaḥ samantaraśmyudgataśrīkūṭarājāya tathāgatāya / namo vipaśyine tathāgatāya / namaḥ śikhine tathāgatāya / namo viśvabhuve tathāgatāya / namaḥ krakucchandāya tathāgatāya / namaḥ kanakamunaye tathāgatāya / namaḥ kāśyapāya tathāgatāyā / namaḥ śākyamunaye tathāgatāyārhate samyaksambuddhāya / tadyathā Ō
children.translated_text: Homage to those who are rightly practicing! Homage to <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> (Śāriputra), the greatly wise! Homage to the assemblies of great <s>Bodhisattvas</s> headed by the noble <s>Maitreya</s>! Homage to the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, Blessed Ones, headed by <s>Supratiṣṭhitaśailendrarāja</s>! Homage to <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Suvarṇavarṇasupratibhāsavinivartiteśvararāja</s>! Homage to <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Siṃhavikrīḍitarāja</s>! Homage to <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitābha</s>! Homage to <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Supratiṣṭhitamaṇikūṭarāja</s>! Homage to <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Samantaraśmyudgataśrīkūṭarāja</s>! Homage to <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Vipaśyin</s>! Homage to <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śikhin</s>! Homage to <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Viśvabhu</s>! Homage to <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Krakucchanda</s>! Homage to <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Kanakamuni</s>! Homage to <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Kāśyapa</s>! Homage to <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One! The <s>dhāraṇī</s>:

body.translated_text: Then the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, with unblinking eyes, spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'Hear me, O Blessed One! This <s>vimokṣamukhamaṇḍala</s> (circle of the gate of liberation), to which homage has been paid by all <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, is for the benefit of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the welfare, benefit, happiness, and liberation of the great multitude of beings. Homage to all <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who abide established in the three times! Homage to the assemblies of <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> and noble <s>Śrāvakas</s>, past, future, and present! Homage to those who have gone rightly!

body.text: oṃ mune mune mahāmunaye svāhā / oṃ śame śame mahāśame rakṣa rakṣa māṃ sarvasattvāṃś ca sarvapāpaṃ praśamane svāhā / namaḥ suparikīrtitanāmadheyāya tathāgatāya / namaḥ samantāvabhāsavijitasaṃgrāmaśriye tathāgatāya / namaḥ indraketudhvajaśriye tathāgatāya / namo ratnaprabhāseśvararājāya tathāgatāya / namo 'pratihatabhaiṣajyarājāya tathāgatāya / namo vikrāntagāmine tathāgatāya / namo buddhāya / namo dharmāya / namaḥ saṃghāya / namo 'tītānāgatapratyutpannebhyo buddhebhyo bhagavadbhyaḥ / tadyathā Ō
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ mune mune mahāmunaye svāhā</s>! <s>Oṃ śame śame mahāśame rakṣa rakṣa māṃ sarvasattvāṃś ca sarvapāpaṃ praśamane svāhā</s>! Homage to <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Suparikīrtitanāmadheya</s> (Well-Proclaimed Name)! Homage to <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Samantāvabhāsavijitasaṃgrāmaśrī</s> (Glory of Conquest by All-Pervading Radiance)! Homage to <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Indraketudhvajaśrī</s> (Glory of Indra's Banner)! Homage to <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnaprabhāseśvararāja</s> (King Lord of Jewel-Radiance)! Homage to <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Apratihatabhaiṣajyarāja</s> (Unobstructed Medicine King)! Homage to <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Vikrāntagāmin</s> (Valorous Strider)! Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>! Homage to the <s>Dharma</s>! Homage to the <s>Saṃgha</s>! Homage to the <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones of the past, future, and present! The <s>dhāraṇī</s>:

children.text: ) bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya / ebhyo namaskṛtvā idam āryāvalokiteśvaramukhodgīrṇam amoghapāśarājanāma hṛdayaṃ tathāgatasaṃmukhaṃ bhāṣitaṃ mahatparṣanmadhye 'ham idānīm āvartayiṣye / sidhyantu me mantrapadā sarvakāryāṇi sarvabhayebhyo mama sarvasattvānāṃ ca rakṣā bhavatu / tadyathā Ō
children.translated_text: the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, the greatly compassionate one! Having paid homage to these, I shall now recite this <s>Amoghapāśarāja</s>-named <s>hṛdaya</s> (heart-dhāraṇī), proclaimed from the mouth of the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, spoken in the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, in the midst of the great assembly. May my <s>mantra</s>-words be efficacious! May there be protection from all fears for me and for all beings! The <s>dhāraṇī</s>:

body.translated_text: <s>Smṛtivarddhani</s> (increaser of mindfulness), <s>mativarddhani</s> (increaser of intellect), <s>gativarddhani</s> (increaser of progress), <s>dhṛtivarddhani</s> (increaser of steadfastness), <s>prajñāvarddhani</s> (increaser of wisdom), <s>pratibhānavarddhani</s> (increaser of eloquence), <s>dhyānavarddhani</s> (increaser of meditation), <s>samādhivarddhani</s> (increaser of concentration), <s>śamathavarddhani</s> (increaser of calm abiding), <s>vipaśyanāvarddhani</s> (increaser of insight) — increaser of all qualities conducive to awakening (<s>bodhipakṣadharma</s>), for the complete fulfillment of all <s>Buddha</s>-qualities, <s>svāhā</s>! Homage to the Three Jewels! Homage to the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, the greatly compassionate one! Homage to <s>Mahāsthāmaprāpta</s>,

children.text: ) bhagavan somādityayamavaruṇakuberabrahmendravāyvagnidhanada-ṛṣidevagaṇābhyarcitacaraṇa / suru suru curu curu muru muru dhuru dhuru sanatkumārarudravāsavaviṣṇudhanadavāyvagni-ṛṣināyakavināyakabahuvividhaveśadhara / dhara dhara dhiri dhiri dhuru dhuru tara tara thara thara dhara dhara para para lara lara hara hara yara yara sara sara vara vara varadāyaka / samantāvalokitavilokitalokeśvaramaheśvaratribhuvaneśvarasarvaguṇasamalaṅkṛtāvalokiteśvara muhu muhu muru muru muya muya muñca muñca rakṣa rakṣa māṃ sarvasattvāṃś ca sarvabhayebhyaḥ sarvopadravebhyaḥ sarvopasargebhyaḥ sarvagrahebhyaḥ sarvavyādhibhyaḥ sarvaviṣebhyaḥ sarvajvarebhyaḥ / evaṃ bandha bandha tāḍanatarjanarājataskarāgnyudakaviṣaśastraparimocaka / kaṇa kaṇa kiṇi kiṇi kuṇu kuṇu cara cara ciri ciri curu curu indriyabalabodhyaṃgacaturāryasatyasaṃprakāśaka / tapa tapa tama tama dama dama śama śama masa masa dhama dhama mahākāruṇika mahātamondhakāravidhamanaṣaṭpāramitāparipūraka / mala mala mili mili mulu mulu ṭaṭa ṭaṭa ṭhaṭha ṭhaṭha ṭiṭi ṭiṭi ṭhiṭhi ṭhiṭhi ṭuṭu ṭuṭu ṭhuṭhu ṭhuṭhu eṇeyacarmakṛtaparikara ehy ehi mahākāruṇika / īśvaramaheśvaramahābhūtagaṇasaṃbhañjaka / kara kara kiri kiri kuru kuru para para hara hara (
children.translated_text: ) O Blessed One (<s>Bhagavan</s>), whose feet are worshipped by <s>Soma</s>, <s>Āditya</s>, <s>Yama</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Agni</s>, <s>Dhanada</s>, and the hosts of <s>ṛṣis</s> and <s>devas</s>! suru suru curu curu muru muru dhuru dhuru, O Bearer of the manifold forms of <s>Sanatkumāra</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Vāsava</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Dhanada</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Agni</s>, the chief <s>ṛṣis</s>, and <s>Vināyaka</s>! dhara dhara dhiri dhiri dhuru dhuru tara tara thara thara dhara dhara para para lara lara hara hara yara yara sara sara vara vara, O Bestower of Boons (<s>varadāyaka</s>)! O <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, who surveys all directions, who is <s>Lokeśvara</s> (Lord of the World), <s>Maheśvara</s> (Great Lord), <s>Tribhuvaneśvara</s> (Lord of the Three Worlds), adorned with all virtues! muhu muhu muru muru muya muya muñca muñca, protect, protect (<s>rakṣa rakṣa</s>) me and all beings from all fears, from all calamities, from all afflictions, from all seizures (<s>grahas</s>), from all diseases, from all poisons, from all fevers! Thus, bind, bind! O Liberator from striking, threatening, kings, thieves, fire, water, poison, and weapons (<s>tāḍana-tarjana-rāja-taskara-agni-udaka-viṣa-śastra-parimocaka</s>)! kaṇa kaṇa kiṇi kiṇi kuṇu kuṇu cara cara ciri ciri curu curu, O Illuminator of the faculties (<s>indriyas</s>), powers (<s>balas</s>), factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅgas</s>), and the Four Noble Truths (<s>caturāryasatya</s>)! tapa tapa tama tama dama dama śama śama masa masa dhama dhama, O Great Compassionate One, O Dispeller of great darkness and delusion, O Fulfiller of the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections)! mala mala mili mili mulu mulu ṭaṭa ṭaṭa ṭhaṭha ṭhaṭha ṭiṭi ṭiṭi ṭhiṭhi ṭhiṭhi ṭuṭu ṭuṭu ṭhuṭhu ṭhuṭhu, O Wearer of a garment made of antelope skin (<s>eṇeyacarmakṛtaparikara</s>), come, come, O Great Compassionate One! O Destroyer of the hosts of great beings [under] <s>Īśvara</s> and <s>Maheśvara</s>! kara kara kiri kiri kuru kuru para para hara hara (

children.text: ) vara vara sara sara mara mara kara kara kaṭa kaṭa kiṭi kiṭi kuṭu kuṭu maṭa maṭa mahāviśuddhaviṣayanivāsina mahākāruṇika / śvetayajñopavītaratnamukuṭamālādharasarvajñaśirasi kṛtajaṭāmukuṭamahādbhutakamalālaṅkṛtakarataladhyānasamādhivimokṣāprakampya bahusattvasaṃtatiparipālakamahākāruṇika sarvakarmāvaraṇaviśodhaka sarvajñajñānaparipūraka sarvavyādhivimocaka sarvasattvāśāparipūrakasarvasattvasamāśvāsanakara namo 'stu te svāhā / amoghāya svāhā / amoghapāśāya svāhā / ajitāya svāhā / aparājitāya svāhā / amitābhāya svāhā / amitābhasutāya svāhā / mārasainyapramardanāya svāhā / abhayāya abhayapradāya svāhā / jayāya svāhā / vijayāya svāhā / jayavijayāya svāhā / varadāya svāhā / varapradāya svāhā / akālamṛtyupraśamanāya svāhā / idaṃ ca me karma kuru namo 'stu te svāhā / oṃ raṇa raṇa hūṃ phaṭ* svāhā / oṃ jaya hūṃ phaṭ* svahā / oṃ jra jiṃ juṃ phaṭ* svāha / oṃ hūṃ jaya svāhā / oṃ hrīḥ trailokyavijayāmoghapāśāpratihata hrīḥ haḥ hūṃ phaṭ* svāhā / oṃ vasumati svāhā / oṃ ārolīk* svāhā / oṃ bahule bahule svāhā / oṃ ārolik* hrīḥ hrīḥ hūṃ phaṭ* svāhā / niyatāniyatavedanīyāśubhasya me bhagavan karmaṇo 'śeṣataḥ parikṣayaṃ kuru svāhā / padmahastāya svāhā / oṃ buddhadharmasaṃghāya svāhā / paṭhitasiddhasyāsya mantrasya karmāṇi bhavanti / (
children.translated_text: <s>vara vara sara sara mara mara kara kara kaṭa kaṭa kiṭi kiṭi kuṭu kuṭu maṭa maṭa</s> — O you who dwell in the realm of great purity! O greatly compassionate one! O you who wear the white sacred thread, jewel crown, and garland, who are omniscient! Upon whose head matted hair is piled in a crown, whose lotus-adorned palms are magnificent, who are unwavering in <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), and <s>vimokṣa</s> (liberation)! O greatly compassionate one who protects the continuity of many beings! O purifier of all <s>karmāvaraṇa</s> (karmic obscurations)! O fulfiller of omniscient knowledge! O liberator from all diseases! O fulfiller of all beings' hopes! O comforter of all beings! Homage to you, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Amogha</s> (the Infallible), <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Amoghapāśa</s> (the Infallible Lasso), <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Ajita</s> (the Unconquered), <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Aparājita</s> (the Undefeated), <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Amitābha</s> (Infinite Light), <s>svāhā</s>! To the son of <s>Amitābha</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To the crusher of <s>Māra's</s> armies, <s>svāhā</s>! To the fearless one, the giver of fearlessness, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Jayā</s> (Victory), <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Vijayā</s> (Conquest), <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Jayavijaya</s> (Victory and Conquest), <s>svāhā</s>! To the giver of boons, <s>svāhā</s>! To the bestower of boons, <s>svāhā</s>! To the pacifier of untimely death, <s>svāhā</s>! Accomplish this action of mine — homage to you, <s>svāhā</s>! <s>Oṃ raṇa raṇa hūṃ phaṭ svāhā</s>! <s>Oṃ jaya hūṃ phaṭ svāhā</s>! <s>Oṃ jra jiṃ juṃ phaṭ svāhā</s>! <s>Oṃ hūṃ jaya svāhā</s>! <s>Oṃ hrīḥ trailokyavijayāmoghapāśāpratihata hrīḥ haḥ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā</s>! <s>Oṃ vasumati svāhā</s>! <s>Oṃ ārolik svāhā</s>! <s>Oṃ bahule bahule svāhā</s>! <s>Oṃ ārolik hrīḥ hrīḥ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā</s>! O Blessed One, bring about the complete exhaustion of my unwholesome <s>karma</s>, both that which is fixed and unfixed in its retribution, without remainder, <s>svāhā</s>! To the lotus-handed one, <s>svāhā</s>! <s>Oṃ</s> — to <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṃgha</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! When this <s>mantra</s> has been recited and accomplished, its ritual acts come into effect.

children.text: ) trikālajāpena pañcānantaryāṇi śodhayati / sarvakarmāvaraṇāni viśuddhiṃ ca karoti / agarudhūpena sīmābandhaḥ bhasmodakena sarṣapakhadirakīlakādyaiḥ sarvajvareṣu sūtrakaṃ bandhayitavyam* / sarvavyādhiṣu ghṛtatailamudakaṃ vā parijapya dātavyam* / kākhordacchedanaṃ śastreṇa rakṣāsūtrakaṃ ca / udaraśūlena lavaṇodakaṃ viṣanāśanaṃ mṛttikayā udakena vā / cakṣurogeṇa śvetasūtrakaṃ karṇe bandhayitavyam* / dantaśūlena karavīradantakāṣṭhakam* / sīmābandhaṃ pañcaraṅgikasūtram ekaviṃśativārān parijapya caturṣu khadirakīlakeṣu baddhvā caturdiśaṃ nikhātavyaṃ sīmābandho bhaviṣyati / sarvarakṣāsūtrakenodakena bhasmena vā / sarvagraheṣu pañcaraṅgikasūtrakam* / sarvajvareṣu śvetasūtrakaṃ sarpakīṭāḥ lūtalohaliṃgagalagraheṣu madhupippalīyutam* / cakṣuroge gandhodakapalāśodakaṃ madhuyaṣṭyudakaṃ vā sarvakalikalahavivādebhyaḥ abhyākhyāneṣūdakaṃ parijapya mukhaṃ prakṣālayitavyam* / paraviṣayarājyopadravarāṣṭrakeṣu pūrṇakalaśaṃ sthāpayitvā śucinā śucivastraprāvṛtena mahatīṃ pūjāṃ kṛtvā vācayitavyaṃ mahāśāntir bhavati / tena codakena sektavyaṃ sarvasattvānāṃ rakṣā kṛtā bhavati / sarvety upadravopasargāḥ praśāmyanti / mudritāṃ candanatilakaṃ hṛdaye ekaviṃśativārān parijapya kartavyaṃ sarvānantaryāṇi kṣayaṃ yānti / satatajāpena gṛharakṣā / padmahomena sarvasattvarakṣā / candanahomena sarvagrahabhūtanakṣatrarakṣā / jayāvijayā-aparājitā nākulī gandhanākūlī dhāraṇī abhayapāṇi indriyapāṇigandhapriyaṃgutagaracakrā mahācakrā vikrāntāsomarājī sunandā ceti / yathā saṃbhavata aṣṭottaraśatavārān parijapya maṇiṃ kṛtvā śirasi bāhau vā dhārayitavyam* / bālānāṃ gale nārīṇāṃ vilagne svayaṃ paraṃ saubhāgyakaram* / (
children.translated_text: Through recitation at the three times of day, the five <s>ānantarya</s> (heinous) sins are purified. All <s>karmāvaraṇas</s> (karmic obscurations) are purified. With <s>agaru</s> (aloe-wood) incense, a boundary-binding [is accomplished]. With ash-water, mustard seeds, <s>khadira</s> (acacia) pegs, and the like, a cord should be tied for all fevers. For all diseases, ghee, oil, or water should be consecrated [with the mantra] and given. For removing <s>kākhorda</s> (sorcery), [use] a blade and a protective cord. For stomach pain, salt-water. For destroying poison, [use] clay or water. For eye disease, a white cord should be tied on the ear. For toothache, [use] an oleander tooth-stick. For a boundary-binding, a five-colored cord should be consecrated twenty-one times, tied to four <s>khadira</s> pegs, and driven into the four directions — a boundary-binding will come into effect. For all protection, [use] a cord, water, or ash. For all planetary afflictions, a five-colored cord. For all fevers, a white cord. For snake, insect, spider, <s>lohaliṅga</s>, and throat-seizure afflictions, [use a remedy] mixed with honey and long pepper. For eye disease, scented water, <s>palāśa</s>-wood water, or licorice water. For all quarrels, disputes, and conflicts, and in legal accusations, water should be consecrated and used to wash the face. In foreign lands, kingdoms, or troubled realms, a full water-pot should be established, and having covered it with a clean cloth, a great worship should be performed and the [mantra] recited — a great pacification comes about. With that water, [the area] should be sprinkled — protection for all beings is accomplished. All calamities and afflictions are pacified. A <s>candana</s> (sandalwood) mark should be made on the heart [of the image] while consecrating it twenty-one times — all <s>ānantarya</s> (heinous) sins are destroyed. Through constant recitation, protection of the home [is achieved]. Through a lotus <s>homa</s> (fire oblation), protection of all beings. Through a sandalwood <s>homa</s>, protection from all planetary and spirit afflictions. <s>Jayā</s>, <s>Vijayā</s>, <s>Aparājitā</s>, <s>Nākulī</s>, fragrant <s>Nākulī</s>, <s>Dhāraṇī</s>, <s>Abhayapāṇi</s>, <s>Indriyapāṇi</s>, fragrance, <s>priyangu</s>, <s>tagara</s>, <s>cakrā</s>, <s>mahācakrā</s>, <s>vikrāntā</s>, <s>somarājī</s>, <s>sunandā</s> — these [herbs and substances], as available, should be consecrated one hundred and eight times, made into an amulet, and worn on the head or arm. For children, [tied] around the neck; for women, worn upon the body — it produces good fortune for oneself and others.

children.text:
) alakṣmīpraśamanaṃ putradaṃ ca / etena maṇinā baddhena sarvarakṣā kṛtā bhavati / viṣāgninā na kramati viṣakṛtaṃ notpadyate / utpannāpi na pīḍāṃ janayiṣyati śīghraṃ praśamayiṣyanti / grahān praśamayiṣyati vātameghāśanistambhanaṃ vāriṇā karavīralatayā sarvakarmakaram* / āryāvalokiteśvarahṛdayaṃ paramasiddham asādhitam ete tāni karmāṇi kurute / atha sādhayitum icchan vidhiḥ paṭe 'śeṣakair varṇakair buddhapratimālikhyāryāvalokiteśvaro jaṭāmukuṭadhārī eṇeyacarmakṛtaparivāsā paśupativeśadharaḥ sarvālaṅkārabhūṣitaṃ kṛtvā poṣadhikena citrakareṇa
citrāpayitavyaḥ / tataḥ sādhakena tasyāgrato 'patitagomayena maṇḍalaṃ kṛtvā śvetapuṣpāvakīrṇam aṣṭāu gandhodakapūrṇakumbhāḥ sthāpayitavyāḥ / aṣṭāv upahārāś catuṣaṣṭir upakaraṇāni / balimāṃsarudhiravarjitaḥ agarudhūpaṃ dahatā vidyāṣṭasahasrajāpayitavyā / ahorātroṣitena vā trirātroṣitena vā triśuklabhojitā vā trikālasnāpayitā śucivastraprāvṛto bhūtvā jāpo dātavyaḥ / tataḥ pratimāyā agrataḥ ātmānaṃ ca likhitaṃ paśyati taṃ dṛṣṭvā ca prahṛṣyati yāvat svayam evāryāvalokiteśvara āgacchati / sarvāśā paripūrayati / manaḥśilāñjanaṃ vā parijapya akṣiṇy aṃjayitvā tato 'ntarhito bhavati / ākāśe krāmati / asaṃmohajñānavyūhanāma samādhiṃ pratilabhate / yad icchati tat karoty eva sādhaka iti /
children.translated_text: ) it pacifies misfortune and bestows sons. When this gem (<s>maṇi</s>) is bound on, complete protection is accomplished. Poison and fire do not affect [the wearer]; what is caused by poison does not arise; and even if it has arisen, it shall cause no pain — they shall quickly pacify it. It shall pacify the <s>grahas</s> (seizing-spirits); for the stopping of wind, clouds, and thunderbolts, [it is used] with water and oleander vine — it does all deeds. The <s>Āryāvalokiteśvarahṛdaya</s>, supremely accomplished and [itself] unaccomplished [by external means], performs these deeds. Now the rite for one wishing to accomplish [it]: on a cloth, with all the [requisite] pigments, having drawn an image of the <s>Buddha</s> and the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> wearing a matted-hair crown (<s>jaṭāmukuṭa</s>), with the upper garment made of antelope skin, bearing the guise of <s>Paśupati</s>, adorned with all ornaments — it should be painted by a painter who keeps the fasting observance (<s>poṣadha</s>). Then by the practitioner, having made before it a <s>maṇḍala</s> of fresh cow-dung not fallen [to the ground], strewn with white flowers, eight pots filled with scented water should be placed; eight offerings and sixty-four [ritual] requisites [should be arranged]. Avoiding sacrificial-cake, meat, and blood, while burning <s>agaru</s> (aloe-wood) incense, the <s>vidyā</s> (spell) should be recited eight thousand times. Fasting for a day and a night, or for three nights, or eating [pure food] for three [days of the] bright fortnight, or bathing at the three times, having become clothed in pure garments, the recitation should be performed. Then before the image he sees himself also drawn [in the painting]; and seeing it he rejoices, until the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> himself comes. He fulfills all wishes. Or, having consecrated <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar) and collyrium and smeared it on the eyes, one then becomes invisible; one moves through the sky; one attains the <s>samādhi</s> named <s>Asaṃmohajñānavyūha</s> (Array of Non-Deluded Knowledge); whatever the practitioner wishes, that he indeed does.

body.translated_text: Oṃ cara cara ciri ciri curu curu mara mara miri miri muru muru, O Great Compassionate One (<s>mahākāruṇika</s>)! sara sara siri siri suru suru curu curu ciri ciri viri viri miri miri, O Great Lotus-Handed One (<s>mahāpadmahasta</s>)! kala kala kili kili kulu kulu, O Great Pure Being (<s>mahāśuddhasattva</s>)! buddhya buddhya bodha bodha bodhi bodhi bodhaya bodhaya kaṇa kaṇa kiṇi kiṇi kuṇu kuṇu, O Supremely Pure Being (<s>paramaśuddhasattva</s>)! kara kara kiri kiri kuru kuru, O <s>Mahāsthāmaprāpta</s> (One Who Has Attained Great Power)! cala cala saṃcala saṃcala vicala vicala pracala pracala eṭaṭa eṭaṭa bhara bhara bhiri bhiri bhuru bhuru tara tara tiri tiri turu turu, come, come, O Great Compassionate One! O Bearer of the form of <s>Mahāpaśupati</s> (the Great Lord of Beasts)! dhara dhara dhiri dhiri dhuru dhuru tara tara sara sara cara cara para para vara vara mara mara lara lara hara hara hāhā hīhī hūhū, O Bearer of the form of <s>Oṃkāra-Brahmā</s>! dhara dhara dhiri dhiri dhuru dhuru tara tara sara sara cara cara nara nara vara vara hara hara, O One whose body is adorned with a hundred thousand rays (<s>raśmiśatasahasrapratimaṇḍitaśarīra</s>)! jvala jvala tapa tapa bhāsa bhāsa bhrama bhrama (

body.text: idam avocad bhagavān āttamanā āryāvalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvas te ca bhikṣavas te ca bodhisattvās te śuddhāvāsakāyikā devaputrāḥ sadevamānuṣāsuragandharvaś ca loko bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandann iti /
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said this, and the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, delighted in mind, and those monks, and those <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and those <s>devaputras</s> of the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> (Pure Abodes) host, and the world with its gods, humans, <s>asuras</s>, and <s>gandharvas</s>, rejoiced at the speech of the Blessed One.
// Here ends the noble <s>Mahāyāna sūtra</s> named <s>Amoghapāśahṛdaya</s>. //
